whats_new: In the desktop app, + opens a ZTC tab, and the ▾ beside it opens new tabs and splits of ZTC, Claude Code, Codex or a shell.
Cmd+D now splits a shell; Ctrl+Cmd+Z, A and O split ZTC, Claude Code and Codex, and Ctrl+Cmd+N opens the new-pane menu.
/provider lists Zerg Router's providers and your own keys, with what each needs, and switches this pane and new panes in one step.
The desktop app's model chip asks for the provider first, and switching back to a provider brings back the model you last used with it.
changes: A ZTC pane started on your own key can switch to a provider only Zerg Router serves.
A new tab starts on the provider another pane switched to.
A ZTC or shell pane the desktop app can't open says why.
/models set saves the provider with the model.
The desktop app's new-tab menu stays open after the click that opens it.
An open menu in the desktop app keeps the clicks and keys meant for it.
A desktop pane's header shows the pane's name, not the title its program sets.
A desktop key binding with a word the app doesn't know binds nothing.
A model only Zerg Router serves tells you how to reach it.
A reasoning level a Zerg Router model doesn't offer is refused where you set it.
The desktop app's model chip changes provider.
Switching back to a provider lands on the model you last used with it
The desktop app's tab strip has a ▾ next to its +, for new tabs and splits of every kind.
Signed in to Zerg Router, ZTC refreshes Router's list at startup even when you work on your own key
Cmd+D in the desktop app splits the focused pane with a shell, as in iTerm2 and Ghostty.
